To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the relation between equity incentives and earnings management through permanently reinvested foreign earnings (PRE) is positive for U.S. firms with high foreign sales and negative for U.S. multinationals with low foreign sales.

the relation between equity incentives and earnings management through the use of PRE is stronger when the firm is more profitable, has higher levels of debt, is less diversified, has a larger foreign presence, and is more growth-oriented.
The results are robust to the inclusion of a variety of control variables and alternative measures of earnings management and equity incentives.
